adverse_or_null_results: The Cedar transfer attempt is null/adverse: all five native fixtures and 15 requests passed, but the corpus exposed no independently authored evidence-authority, license, or retraction field.
The zero-request Rust path-binding failure produced no Cedar policy evaluation and remains a setup failure rather than transfer evidence.
Re-execution of the usable OpenSSL verification table agreed on 186 of 191 rows; the five FIPS-provider disagreements remain counted and full reproduction is not claimed.
The origin-witness policy's zero unsafe merges and zero needless rejections are analytic identities because the policy equals the parent-authorized set; they are not detector-performance evidence.
Origin-witness evaluation requires 3,924 parent evaluations across 1,962 tasks, exactly twice the 1,962 native evaluations required by one merged-store policy.
The 46 hybrid authorizations are a frozen third-party-corpus obstruction, not an estimate of production prevalence, deployment risk, security benefit, or human usability.
Forty-five of the 46 hybrids depend on native policy decisions that the structural model does not reproduce; the result remains conditional on the pinned OpenSSL corpus and engine semantics.
The Cedar, Lean, full OpenSSL aggregate replay, and uncommitted per-task verdict routes retain the exact CANNOT_CHECK boundaries documented by the artifact.
The independent in-repository evaluator is implementation-level corroboration, not external human review or cross-institution replication.
The authored split-chain hostile case is a mechanics control only and is not an independent natural observation.
Generic fixed-point, Datalog, provenance-semiring, truth-maintenance, minimal-support, causality, and deletion-robustness mathematics remain donor-owned and are not claimed as new.

The bounded system does not establish cross-institution scientific authority, broad security validity, probabilistic evidence handling, arbitrary negation, inconsistency handling, or deployed reliability.
scientific_mass.dependence_notes: The 1,962 tasks share one OpenSSL source corpus, one engine version and a constructed merge design; they are not a population sample. The 46 hybrids are outcomes within that frozen task set. The formal propositions share one algebra and are not counted as independent empirical observations.
scientific_mass.failure_opportunities: The proof-tree equivalence, unsupported-cycle bottom, refutation monotonicity and cap nonpromotion could each fail on finite countermodels. Native corpus anchoring could disagree, hybrid obstruction could be absent, controls could fail, and comparator costs could erase the practical distinction; recorded disagreements and CANNOT_CHECK routes remain visible.
scientific_mass.independent_unit_type: registered OpenSSL parent-store merge task within one pinned third-party corpus; formal results are linked theorem consequences rather than empirical N

sibling_overlap.merge_test: ORION-03 uniquely studies evidence-license propagation/nonpromotion in finite positive rule graphs and one origin-mixing instantiation. Broader authority governance and execution-integrity siblings do not own this theorem-plus-obstruction object.

surviving_claim.plain_language: In a finite positive conjunctive rule system, evidence licenses propagate only when every premise and the rule cap permit them; this gives exact fail-closed nonpromotion and refutation semantics, while a frozen OpenSSL corpus shows a bounded origin-mixing obstruction and its evaluation cost.
surviving_claim.posterior_change: Boolean reachability is insufficient for evidence-bearing records: a finite typed-license algebra can make nonpromotion and post-refutation survival executable, and erasing origin can create native-engine authorizations that neither parent source permits.
